title: New chart type: Gauge (S2)

complexity.rationale: A wholly new mark type with no existing precedent in either package: arc/track rendering, needle-vs-fill mode, sequential threshold zone coloring, target markers, tick decoration, and responsive named sizing are each genuinely new, non-precedented logic, not a repeat of an existing pattern. Donut supplies an arc-geometry precedent and Bullet supplies a threshold/target API precedent, but neither covers needle rendering, threshold-to-arc-zone coloring, or the fill/needle mode switch, so multiple sites each need different new reasoning. Remaining research also includes whether BigNumber/Bullet S2 prerequisites are needed first, and no Figma detail was available in this investigation.

summary: Add a Gauge chart type to react-spectrum-charts-s2 that shows a single metric value within a configured range via an arc track, either with a needle pointing at the value (colored by sequential thresholds) or a colored arc fill from the range minimum to the current value. Confirmed via grep that no gauge component or mark exists anywhere in packages/react-spectrum-charts-s2/src or packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src today.
requirements: Render a full prop set: name, label (required, shown in center), metric (default 'value'), minScaleValue (default 0), maxScaleValue (default 100), method ('last'|'avg'|'sum', default 'last'), numberFormat (default 'shortNumber'), showNeedle (default true), color (default 'categorical-01'), arcSize (default 2/3, range 0.2-0.85), holeRatio (default 0.8, range 0.4-0.9), thresholds, target, targetLabel, ticks, showRangeLabels (default false), size ('XL'|'L'|'M'|'S'|number, default 'M').
Always render the label and the aggregated, formatted metric value in the center of the arc.
When showNeedle is true, color the arc track in sequential threshold zones (or a single color if no thresholds are set) and render a needle pointing at the aggregated value.
When showNeedle is false, fill the arc from minScaleValue to the aggregated current value using the color prop; thresholds do not apply to fill-mode coloring per the issue's spec.
Ignore the color prop when thresholds are set (needle mode only), following the same precedence Bullet already uses for thresholdBarColor vs. thresholds.

Treat thresholds as sequential, non-overlapping zones aligned with Bullet's ThresholdBackground shape (packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src/types/marks/bulletSpec.types.ts), auto-showing each threshold's breakpoint value only when that threshold entry has a label.
Support target/targetLabel data keys aligned with Bullet's existing target/targetLabel API.
Clamp values outside [minScaleValue, maxScaleValue] silently for rendering, but emit a dev-facing console.error when clamping occurs.
Support ticks ('minimal'|'normal'|'dense'), off by default, as decorative marks only (no data encoding).
Support showRangeLabels to render minScaleValue/maxScaleValue labels at the arc endpoints.
Support the named/numeric size prop (XL=350px, L=225px, M=150px, S=110px, or an explicit number) the same way other S2 chart-level sizing works.
Accept <ChartTooltip> as a child following the standard RSC child-component pattern (see donutAdapter.ts's popover/tooltip child handling for precedent).
Fix the track color to a Spectrum neutral token rather than a user-configurable color, per the issue's spec.
Treat arcSize and holeRatio as chart-author-only configuration, not exposed as end-user runtime controls.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: clamp silently to the nearest bound for rendering position, but log a dev-facing console.error so the chart author notices the mismatch

edgeCases.case: no data or the metric field is missing/empty
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: render the label with an empty/placeholder value rather than throwing, consistent with how BigNumber-style single-value marks in this codebase should degrade

edgeCases.case: thresholds overlap or are supplied out of order
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: normalize/sort by value before rendering zones; document that overlapping thresholds are not supported input, mirroring Bullet's existing 'sequential, non-overlapping' threshold contract

edgeCases.case: long label, targetLabel, or threshold label text at small sizes (size='S', 110px)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: truncate with an ellipsis rather than overflowing the fixed-size container, consistent with existing S2 label-truncation conventions

edgeCases.case: size set to a custom number smaller than the smallest named size (110px)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: arc/needle/tick/label geometry all scale down proportionally rather than clipping or overlapping
the fixed neutral track color and any background/halo behind the needle must resolve via the existing BACKGROUND_COLOR signal convention, not a hardcoded color value

edgeCases.case: showNeedle true with no thresholds set
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: the arc renders in the single color prop value rather than defaulting to an empty/uncolored track

edgeCases.case: hover/tooltip interaction over the arc or needle
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: ChartTooltip, if present, follows the same interactive-mark (isInteractive) wiring as other S2 marks rather than a bespoke hover path

crossCutting.notes: touchesTooltipOrPopover: the issue explicitly requires accepting <ChartTooltip> as a child, following the standard RSC interactive-mark pattern. requiresNewSignalOrScale: mapping a metric value to an arc angle/needle rotation needs a new scale (linear value -> angle) and likely a reactive signal for the aggregated/clamped value, neither of which exists in any current mark. requiresS1S2Parity is false because this is explicitly an S2-alpha-only feature with no S1 vega-spec-builder equivalent planned.

implementationPlan.change: New file. Define GaugeOptions (public contract) and GaugeSpecOptions (defaults-applied + internal fields), modeled on donutSpec.types.ts's pattern, reusing Bullet's ThresholdBackground-style shape (bulletSpec.types.ts) for thresholds and target/targetLabel.
New file. Add the produce-wrapped addGauge function (assembles defaults, calls addData/addSignals/setScales/addGaugeMarks), modeled on donut/donutSpecBuilder.ts's addDonut.
New file. Arc/needle geometry helpers (arcSize/holeRatio math, value-to-angle mapping, threshold-zone-to-arc-segment coloring), modeled on donut/donutUtils.ts's arc geometry helpers.
New file. Test fixtures for GaugeSpecOptions variants, modeled on donut/donutTestUtils.ts.
Wire in a case for the new Gauge mark type calling addGauge, following the existing pattern used for addDonut/addBullet.
New file. GaugeProps (React boundary), modeled on donut.types.ts's Omit-based pattern over GaugeOptions.
New file. Render-null prop-holder component carrying default values, modeled on rc/components/Donut/Donut.tsx.
New file. childrenAdapter case for Gauge.displayName, including ChartTooltip child handling, modeled on rscToSbAdapter/donutAdapter.ts.
New file. Storybook stories covering needle mode, fill mode, thresholds, target, ticks, and each named size, modeled on stories/components/Donut/Donut.story.tsx.

openQuestions: schema.json's chartType enum (area/bar/bigNumber/bullet/combo/donut/line/scatter/venn/chart) has no 'gauge' value; a real implementation PR needs to add 'gauge' before a proper chartType-scoped spec directory (planning/specs/gauge/...) can be used instead of the generic 'chart' fallback used here.

BigNumber S2 support is currently only a types stub (packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src/types/marks/bigNumberSpec.types.ts, with no spec builder or React component found under either package's src) — does Gauge's center label/value rendering need BigNumber's number-formatting utilities to land first, or can Gauge inline its own numberFormat handling independently?

Bullet has no React component wrapper yet in react-spectrum-charts-s2/src (only its vega-spec-builder-s2 spec builder exists) — should Gauge's target/threshold API wait for Bullet's own React component to land first for API consistency, or proceed now and reconcile later?
The original issue's Figma link was not accessible in this investigation — exact arc styling, needle shape, and tick appearance need designer confirmation before implementation.

Should arcSize/holeRatio being 'chart-author-only' be enforced purely via omission from the public TypeScript GaugeProps, or does it also need a runtime dev warning for untyped/JS consumers who pass it anyway?
